content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-17
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-17
14	
15	- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
19	
20	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
21	
22	### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)
23	
24	A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.
25	
26	**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.
27	
28	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.
29	
30	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
31	
32	1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
33	2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
34	3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.
35	
36	---
37	
38	### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)
39	
40	A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.
41	
42	**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.
43	
44	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.
45	
46	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
47	
48	1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
49	2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
64	2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.
65	
66	---
67	
68	### User Story 4 - The synchronization badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (Priority: P3)
69	
70	While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.
71	
72	**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.
73	
74	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77	
78	1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
79	2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.
80	
81	---
82	
83	### Edge Cases
84	
85	- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
86	- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
87	- The most recent page of entries is itself empty (e.g., nothing happened today or yesterday) while the account has entries further back: paging continues to load those older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
88	- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.
89	- The user reaches the end of their history: the list simply stops loading further pages without an error, with no "end of list" case to treat as a failure.
90	
91	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
92	
93	### Functional Requirements
94	
95	- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).
96	- **FR-002**: Entries MUST be grouped under date headings by the calendar day they occurred ("Hoje" for today, "Ontem" for yesterday, an explicit date for anything older), with date groups ordered newest-to-oldest and, within each group, entries ordered newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time; each entry MUST be rendered as a card showing: a marker and icon distinguishing its origin, its time, a text excerpt, any attached tags as read-only chips (only when present), and a per-entry synchronization badge.
97	- **FR-003**: The system MUST support browsing the user's complete entry history beyond what fits in a single fetch, loading further entries automatically as the user scrolls, and appending them without disturbing already-rendered cards or the user's current scroll position.
98	- **FR-004**: When the signed-in user has zero entries, the screen MUST show an empty state (illustration, "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action) instead of an empty list; completing a save from that action MUST return the user to this screen with the new entry visible in its correct date group.
99	- **FR-005**: The per-entry synchronization badge MUST independently reflect exactly one of three states — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed for each entry from its own server-confirmed data together with the device's own knowledge of any write still pending or unreconciled for that entry, following the sync-badge semantics; this computation and its on-screen state MUST NOT depend on, be blocked by, or be delayed by session or authentication handling (login, silent renewal, or the expired-session overlay).
100	- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.

120	- **SC-004**: When a session expires while a user is viewing this screen, 100% of the time their loaded entries and scroll position are unchanged after they re-authenticate.

# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: When this screen merges the entry RF01's save flow already placed in the app's local in-memory entries store with the entries this screen fetches from the backend, how should it avoid showing that same entry twice? → A: Dedupe by entry ID. RF01's save flow only adds an entry to the local store after the backend has confirmed the write, so every locally-held entry already carries a real, server-issued ID; when a fetched backend page returns an entry whose ID already exists in the local store, the two are recognized as the same entry and shown once (preferring the freshly-fetched copy's confirmation data — `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` — since it is at least as current as the local one). This is the simplest reliable key available and is what keeps SC-001's "100% of entries appear exactly once" true once a locally-created entry's page is later re-fetched from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: Within each date group (and across date groups), in what order are entries displayed — and does that order match the order newer pages get appended to older ones while scrolling? → A: Reverse-chronological throughout: date groups run newest-to-oldest ("Hoje" at the very top), and within each group entries run newest-to-oldest by their occurrence time. This matches the backend's cursor-based pagination (each further page is strictly older than what's already loaded) and the prototype's own "Hoje"/"Ontem"/older-dates ordering, and it is the only ordering under which "scrolling down loads older entries, appended at the bottom" (FR-003, Edge Cases) is coherent without resorting already-rendered cards. Neither the prototype extract nor `requirements.md` states this explicitly, so this is a reasonable technical decision per Constitution Principle I rather than an invented behavior with no basis in the frozen inputs. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)

A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.

---

### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)

A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.

**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.

---

### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)

A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.

**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.

---

### User Story 4 - The synchronization badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (Priority: P3)

While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.

**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.

---

### Edge Cases

- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
- The most recent page of entries is itself empty (e.g., nothing happened today or yesterday) while the account has entries further back: paging continues to load those older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.
- The user reaches the end of their history: the list simply stops loading further pages without an error, with no "end of list" case to treat as a failure.

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.
- **FR-010**: This unit MUST NOT implement entry search, text filtering, the category/date/type filter sheet, active-filter chips, export generation, or any other behavior reserved for a later unit (RF05, RF06, or any later RF) or for an extension feature (requirements section 2).

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

27

30	authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
31	functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery

36	technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity

81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90

92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108

112

115	  loading indicator.

117	  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
118	  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.

120	  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
121	- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
122	  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
123	- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose

1	# Synchronization badge semantics
2	
3	There is no `sync_status` column in the database: the architecture is cloud-only, so "it is on the server" already means "synchronized", by definition. The server neither stores nor computes a synchronization state; it only exposes two fields, and the **badge is derived entirely in the app** from them:
4	
5	| Field | Where it appears in the contract | Meaning |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| `updatedAt` | `Entry.updatedAt` | Timestamp of the last server write for that entry. |
8	| `serverRevision` | `Entry.serverRevision`, and also in the profile | Counter that increases with every write to the user's entries — never resets, never decreases. |
9	
10	**The badge's 3 states, all inferred on the client — none comes ready from the server:**
11	1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
12	2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
13	3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.
14	
15	When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

# Synchronization badge semantics

There is no `sync_status` column in the database: the architecture is cloud-only, so "it is on the server" already means "synchronized", by definition. The server neither stores nor computes a synchronization state; it only exposes two fields, and the **badge is derived entirely in the app** from them:

| Field | Where it appears in the contract | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `updatedAt` | `Entry.updatedAt` | Timestamp of the last server write for that entry. |
| `serverRevision` | `Entry.serverRevision`, and also in the profile | Counter that increases with every write to the user's entries — never resets, never decreases. |

**The badge's 3 states, all inferred on the client — none comes ready from the server:**
1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.

When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---

95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

103	| ID | Requirement | Target |

1	# Contract: `SessionRepository` (`lib/features/session/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`)
2	
3	Domain-layer interface owning the session lifecycle: launch-time check, silent refresh, and
4	reading/clearing the stored session. `SessionBloc` depends on this and on nothing in
5	`session/data/` or `auth/data/` directly (RNF06).
6	
7	```dart
8	abstract class SessionRepository {
9	  Future<Either<Failure, Session>> checkSession();     // GET auth-session, using the stored accessToken
10	  Future<Either<Failure, Session>> refresh();           // POST auth-refresh, using the stored refreshToken
11	  Future<void> persist(Session session);                 // write-through to SecureTokenStorage
12	  Future<void> clear();                                   // logout / failed-refresh cleanup
13	  Future<bool> hasStoredSession();                        // true iff a refreshToken is present on device
14	}
15	```
16	
17	- **`checkSession`** → FR-009's first step. `Left(AuthExpiredFailure)` is the expected, non-error
18	  trigger for the caller (`CheckSessionUseCase`) to then call `refresh()` — not itself a terminal
19	  failure shown to the user.
20	- **`refresh`** → FR-009's renewal step, also reused for the silent-refresh-before-overlay path of
21	  FR-013 (User Story 5) and for any later unit's authenticated call that comes back
22	  `AUTH_EXPIRED`. On `Right`, calls `persist()` internally before returning.
23	- **`persist`/`clear`** → thin wrappers over `SecureTokenStorage`; exposed on the repository (not
24	  the data source) so the domain layer's use cases never import `storage/` directly.
25	- **`hasStoredSession`** → lets `CheckSessionUseCase` skip the network call entirely when there is
26	  nothing to check (Edge Cases / User Story 3 scenario 2: no stored session → straight to login,
27	  no call made).
28	
29	## `CheckSessionUseCase` (orchestration, domain layer)
30	
31	```dart
32	Future<SessionStatus> call() async {
33	  if (!await repo.hasStoredSession()) return SessionStatus.unauthenticated;
34	  final checked = await repo.checkSession();
35	  return checked.match(
36	    (failure) => failure is AuthExpiredFailure
37	        ? _tryRefresh()
38	        : SessionStatus.networkError(failure),      // R7 — splash retry affordance, not a route change
39	    (session) => SessionStatus.authenticated(session),
40	  );
41	}
42	
43	Future<SessionStatus> _tryRefresh() async {
44	  final refreshed = await repo.refresh();
45	  return refreshed.match(
46	    (failure) async { await repo.clear(); return SessionStatus.unauthenticated; },
47	    (session) => SessionStatus.authenticated(session),
48	  );
49	}
50	```
51	
52	This single use case is what `SplashPage`/`SessionBloc` calls — it is the only place FR-009's
53	"renew first, then route" rule is implemented, so later units never re-derive it.
54

13:The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).
24:  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
25:  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
29:Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
48:Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.
69:| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
70:| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |
90:| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
91:| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
92:| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
93:| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |
95:### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
171:2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
219:| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
221:| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
226:| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
227:| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |

172	3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.
173	
174	### Micro-animations and transitions
175	- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
176	- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
177	- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
178	- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
179	- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.
180	
181	---
182	
183	## 4. Special states that need extra care
184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195

### 2.6 Plans and settings
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |

Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).

---

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors
| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
|---|---|---|
| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons
Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

1	# Research: P-RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
2	
3	All unknowns this unit raises are implementation judgment calls on top of an already-resolved spec (spec.md's
4	three Clarifications) and an already-built RF01 pipeline — there is no new package, API, or external service
5	to evaluate. Each entry below either corrects an RF01 decision that no longer holds once recognition and save
6	are split apart, or fills a gap spec.md leaves to "reasonable technical decision" (Constitution Principle I).
7	
8	## R1 — Removing the pre-transcription connectivity gate for audio
9	
10	- **Decision**: `AudioTranscriptionRepository.transcribe()` is called unconditionally on `AudioStopRequested`,
11	  with no `ConnectivityChecker` check beforehand. The connectivity gate moves to exactly one place for audio:
12	  immediately before `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`'s `entries-create` call (i.e., when the user taps "Salvar" from
13	  "Áudio — Transcrito").
14	- **Rationale**: RF01's research.md R5 (specs/003) checked connectivity *before* transcription too, but that
15	  was only sound because RF01's single combined usecase would otherwise burn a Whisper inference run for a
16	  save that could never complete regardless. Now that stopping a recording and tapping "Salvar" are two
17	  separate user actions (spec.md FR-001 vs. FR-002), gating transcription itself on connectivity would be
18	  wrong on its own terms: transcription is on-device (Constitution Principle II) and has no network dependency
19	  to protect; blocking it on "offline" would make an unrelated, free local operation fail for no reason, and
20	  would contradict FR-001's unconditional "the system MUST automatically begin on-device transcription" on
21	  stop. The spec's own Edge Cases only ever gate *writes* on connectivity ("'Salvar' ... and 'Salvar só a
22	  foto' both still require connectivity for the underlying `POST /entries` call") — never recognition itself
23	  for audio.
24	- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping RF01's pre-check in front of transcription anyway, "for consistency" —
25	  rejected: it would fail Story 2's Independent Test (forcing a transcription failure) in an environment
26	  that's merely offline but otherwise fine, and silently reclassifies "offline" as a transcription failure
27	  mode it structurally isn't.
28	
29	## R2 — Two new design tokens: the photo thumbnail and the recurring warning icon
30	
31	- **Decision**: Add exactly two entries to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`:
32	  - `sizePhotoThumbnail = 64` — the "small thumbnail" prototype-extract.md §2.3 names for "Foto — Reconhecido"
33	    (next to the editable text) and "Foto — Erro" (kept on screen); one value, reused by both states.
34	  - `sizeStatusIcon = 32` — the red warning icon prototype-extract.md §2.3 names for both "Áudio — Erro" and
35	    "Foto — Erro"; one value, two call sites.
36	- **Rationale**: RF01's research.md R10 (specs/003) found no new token was needed because its own failure UI
37	  was deliberately plain (no icon, no thumbnail — research.md R11). This unit is precisely the one that must
38	  render the prototype's actual "Erro" states, which do name an icon and (for photo) a thumbnail the existing
39	  scale has no equivalent size for — the same bar RF03's research.md R3 (specs/002) already used ("a new token
40	  only when no existing value in the scale fits the exact shape needed, and it's reused at 2+ call sites, not
41	  a one-off"). Both qualify: two states each, not a single use. `colorError` (already present) is reused for
42	  the icon's color and the failure copy — no new color token needed.
43	- **Alternatives considered**: A single shared `sizeWarningIcon`/`sizeThumbnail` combined into one generic
44	  "status visual" token — rejected as it would conflate two different visual roles (an icon vs. an image
45	  thumbnail) for no reuse benefit, since they're never substituted for each other.
46	
47	## R3 — The fixed placeholder content for "Salvar só a foto"
48	
49	- **Decision**: The literal string `'Foto registrada sem texto reconhecido.'` is sent as `content` whenever
50	  "Salvar só a foto" is tapped (`EntrySource.photo`, no further OCR attempt for that capture — FR-008).
51	  Defined as a single `const` in the usecase call site (`InsertionModalBloc`), not duplicated anywhere else.
52	- **Rationale**: spec.md's own resolved Clarification 2 fixes the shape of this requirement (non-empty,
53	  backend-contract-compliant, `source: "photo"`) but explicitly leaves the exact wording to implementation
54	  ("exact wording left to implementation" — spec.md Assumptions). The chosen string is grammatically neutral
55	  Portuguese, describes exactly what happened (an entry was registered from a photo, no text was recognized),
56	  stays well under the 20000-char `content` limit, and is unambiguous if a user later sees it in a future
57	  history/search screen (RF07/RF06) without this unit needing to anticipate that screen's own design.
58	- **Alternatives considered**: Reusing the OCR failure message itself ("Não foi possível reconhecer o texto")
59	  as the stored content — rejected: that sentence describes a *process outcome*, not journal content, and
60	  would read strangely if ever surfaced as an entry's body text in a future timeline view.
61	
62	## R4 — Rendering the prototype's actual "Erro" states, closing RF01's documented carve-out
63	
64	- **Decision**: `CaptureFailureBand` (specs/003's deliberately plain placeholder — generic message + one
65	  outline "Tentar de novo" button, no icon) is removed from `capture_status_views.dart`. A new
66	  `RecognitionErrorView` widget renders prototype-extract.md §2.3's actual "Erro" shape: a
67	  `sizeStatusIcon`-sized warning icon in `colorError`, the exact copy ("Não foi possível transcrever" /
68	  "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto"), an outline "Tentar novamente" button, and — for Foto only — the
69	  secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". `CaptureLoadingIndicator` and `CapturePermissionDeniedMessage` are
70	  unchanged and keep serving their existing, still-applicable roles (the former embeds into the new
71	  "Processando"/"Processando OCR" layouts alongside the frozen waveform/thumbnail; the latter is untouched by
72	  this unit, since Idle/PermissionDenied/Recording/Captura states are RF01's, not RF02's, to redesign).
73	- **Rationale**: This is not a new judgment call so much as carrying out RF01's own research.md R11 (specs/
74	  003) to its stated conclusion: that entry explicitly named the "Erro" states as "RF02's screens to build,"
75	  not an open design question for this unit to re-litigate. spec.md's resolved Clarification 1 confirms it
76	  ("this unit replaces RF01's placeholder recognition UX... with the dedicated states the prototype
77	  defines").
78	- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping `CaptureFailureBand` around for some other, hypothetical use —
79	  rejected: nothing else in this codebase renders it once Áudio/Foto failures move to `RecognitionErrorView`,
80	  and keeping dead code around violates the "don't keep unused code for hypothetical future need" guidance
81	  this plan is held to; it is deleted outright, not deprecated.
82	
83	## R5 — A save-call failure after successful recognition gets its own (non-prototype-named) state, not a reuse of "Erro"
84	
85	- **Decision**: If `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase` fails (offline, or the `entries-create` call itself fails) after
86	  the user taps "Salvar" from "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" — or taps "Salvar só a foto" from "Foto — Erro" — the
87	  bloc emits a new `*SaveFailure` state (`InsertionModalAudioSaveFailure`/`InsertionModalFotoSaveFailure`,
88	  data-model.md) that keeps the reviewed/edited text (and, for photo, the thumbnail) on screen with an inline
89	  error message, rather than falling back to the recognition-failure "Erro" state. Retrying is simply tapping
90	  "Salvar" (or "Salvar só a foto") again — no re-transcription, no re-OCR.
91	- **Rationale**: The prototype's "Erro" states (prototype-extract.md §2.3) are defined specifically for a
92	  *recognition* failure ("Não foi possível transcrever"/"...reconhecer o texto") — spec.md never describes a
93	  distinct screen for "recognition succeeded but the subsequent save failed," leaving this a genuine gap for
94	  reasonable technical judgment (Constitution Principle I). Falling back to "Erro" would be actively wrong
95	  here: it would discard the user's successfully-recognized (and possibly hand-edited) text to show a message
96	  about transcription/OCR, a step that already succeeded. This exactly mirrors an existing, already-approved
97	  precedent in this same codebase: the Texto tab's `InsertionModalTextoFailure` keeps the typed text visible
98	  and treats a second tap of the same "Salvar" button as its own retry (texto_tab_view.dart) — this unit
99	  applies that identical shape to Audio/Foto's post-review save step instead of inventing something new.
100	- **Alternatives considered**: Falling back silently to "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" with no visible error (just
101	  re-enabling "Salvar") — rejected: FR-009's "Erro" precedent and RNF09's "every write endpoint... handled" bar
102	  both imply the user must see *some* failure signal, not a silent no-op. Reusing "Erro" with its recognition
103	  copy substituted for a save-specific message — rejected as a confusing hybrid for the same reason RF01's own
104	  research.md R11 (specs/003) rejected partially borrowing a named state's look.
105	
106	## R6 — Guarding against a stale recognition result after abandonment
107	
108	- **Decision**: Before applying a `transcribe()`/`recognize()` result, the bloc re-checks that its *current*
109	  state is still the matching `*Processing` state for the same held file path (`_pendingAudioPath`/
110	  `_pendingImagePath` unchanged since the call started). If the user has since switched tabs, closed the
111	  modal, or (for photo) retried onto a different in-flight attempt, a late-arriving result is discarded
112	  outright — no state transition, no entry creation.
113	- **Rationale**: spec.md's User Story 5 / Edge Cases requires "no entry is created, regardless of how the
114	  in-flight recognition call eventually resolves," and FR-011 requires discarding "any in-progress
115	  recognition... held for that capture" on abandonment. Switching away from the Áudio/Foto tab already resets
116	  the *visible* state to that tab's idle state (mirroring RF01's existing tab-switch behavior), but without
117	  this explicit guard, a `transcribe()` call that resolves after the switch could still emit
118	  `InsertionModalAudioTranscribed`/`...Failure` and silently clobber whatever the user has navigated to since
119	  — a correctness bug even though `flutter_bloc` v9's post-`close()` emit is already a safe no-op (that only
120	  covers the modal-closed case, not the still-open-but-switched-tabs case).
121	- **Alternatives considered**: Cancelling the underlying `Future` itself (e.g., via a cancellation token passed
122	  into `whisper_ggml`/the OCR call) — rejected as disproportionate: neither `whisper_ggml` nor the OCR HTTP
123	  call exposes a cancellation hook, and the state-match guard achieves the same observable guarantee (no
124	  stray state/entry) without needing one.
125	
126	## R7 — Consolidating `SaveAudioEntryUseCase`/`SavePhotoEntryUseCase` into one `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`
127	
128	- **Decision**: Once recognition is removed from each (R1, and photo's OCR step moving into the new
129	  `RecognizePhotoUseCase`, R-nothing-new beyond what data-model.md documents), `SaveAudioEntryUseCase` and
130	  `SavePhotoEntryUseCase` become identical in every line except the hardcoded `EntrySource` they pass to
131	  `CreateEntryUseCase`. Both are deleted and replaced by one `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase(content, source)` —
132	  connectivity check, then `CreateEntryUseCase(content, source)` — used for Audio-Salvar, Foto-Salvar, and
133	  Foto-"Salvar só a foto" alike (the last simply supplies R3's placeholder string as `content`).
134	- **Rationale**: This is the one place in this unit where two call sites really would be pure duplication of
135	  each other, which is exactly the case where collapsing them is the right amount of abstraction (not a
136	  premature one) — "three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction" cuts the other way once the
137	  lines are not merely similar but identical modulo one parameter already present in the call signature.
138	- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping two thin per-modality usecases "for clarity/discoverability" —
139	  rejected: there is no behavioral difference left to name separately once `EntrySource` is just a parameter,
140	  and two near-identical classes are harder to keep in sync (e.g., a future RNF09 fix applied to one and
141	  missed in the other) than one.

# Research: P-RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing

All unknowns this unit raises are implementation judgment calls on top of an already-resolved spec (spec.md's
three Clarifications) and an already-built RF01 pipeline — there is no new package, API, or external service
to evaluate. Each entry below either corrects an RF01 decision that no longer holds once recognition and save
are split apart, or fills a gap spec.md leaves to "reasonable technical decision" (Constitution Principle I).

## R1 — Removing the pre-transcription connectivity gate for audio

- **Decision**: `AudioTranscriptionRepository.transcribe()` is called unconditionally on `AudioStopRequested`,
  with no `ConnectivityChecker` check beforehand. The connectivity gate moves to exactly one place for audio:
  immediately before `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`'s `entries-create` call (i.e., when the user taps "Salvar" from
  "Áudio — Transcrito").
- **Rationale**: RF01's research.md R5 (specs/003) checked connectivity *before* transcription too, but that
  was only sound because RF01's single combined usecase would otherwise burn a Whisper inference run for a
  save that could never complete regardless. Now that stopping a recording and tapping "Salvar" are two
  separate user actions (spec.md FR-001 vs. FR-002), gating transcription itself on connectivity would be
  wrong on its own terms: transcription is on-device (Constitution Principle II) and has no network dependency
  to protect; blocking it on "offline" would make an unrelated, free local operation fail for no reason, and
  would contradict FR-001's unconditional "the system MUST automatically begin on-device transcription" on
  stop. The spec's own Edge Cases only ever gate *writes* on connectivity ("'Salvar' ... and 'Salvar só a
  foto' both still require connectivity for the underlying `POST /entries` call") — never recognition itself
  for audio.
- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping RF01's pre-check in front of transcription anyway, "for consistency" —
  rejected: it would fail Story 2's Independent Test (forcing a transcription failure) in an environment
  that's merely offline but otherwise fine, and silently reclassifies "offline" as a transcription failure
  mode it structurally isn't.

## R2 — Two new design tokens: the photo thumbnail and the recurring warning icon

- **Decision**: Add exactly two entries to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`:
  - `sizePhotoThumbnail = 64` — the "small thumbnail" prototype-extract.md §2.3 names for "Foto — Reconhecido"
    (next to the editable text) and "Foto — Erro" (kept on screen); one value, reused by both states.
  - `sizeStatusIcon = 32` — the red warning icon prototype-extract.md §2.3 names for both "Áudio — Erro" and
    "Foto — Erro"; one value, two call sites.
- **Rationale**: RF01's research.md R10 (specs/003) found no new token was needed because its own failure UI
  was deliberately plain (no icon, no thumbnail — research.md R11). This unit is precisely the one that must
  render the prototype's actual "Erro" states, which do name an icon and (for photo) a thumbnail the existing
  scale has no equivalent size for — the same bar RF03's research.md R3 (specs/002) already used ("a new token
  only when no existing value in the scale fits the exact shape needed, and it's reused at 2+ call sites, not
  a one-off"). Both qualify: two states each, not a single use. `colorError` (already present) is reused for
  the icon's color and the failure copy — no new color token needed.
- **Alternatives considered**: A single shared `sizeWarningIcon`/`sizeThumbnail` combined into one generic
  "status visual" token — rejected as it would conflate two different visual roles (an icon vs. an image
  thumbnail) for no reuse benefit, since they're never substituted for each other.

## R3 — The fixed placeholder content for "Salvar só a foto"

- **Decision**: The literal string `'Foto registrada sem texto reconhecido.'` is sent as `content` whenever
  "Salvar só a foto" is tapped (`EntrySource.photo`, no further OCR attempt for that capture — FR-008).
  Defined as a single `const` in the usecase call site (`InsertionModalBloc`), not duplicated anywhere else.
- **Rationale**: spec.md's own resolved Clarification 2 fixes the shape of this requirement (non-empty,
  backend-contract-compliant, `source: "photo"`) but explicitly leaves the exact wording to implementation
  ("exact wording left to implementation" — spec.md Assumptions). The chosen string is grammatically neutral
  Portuguese, describes exactly what happened (an entry was registered from a photo, no text was recognized),
  stays well under the 20000-char `content` limit, and is unambiguous if a user later sees it in a future
  history/search screen (RF07/RF06) without this unit needing to anticipate that screen's own design.
- **Alternatives considered**: Reusing the OCR failure message itself ("Não foi possível reconhecer o texto")
  as the stored content — rejected: that sentence describes a *process outcome*, not journal content, and
  would read strangely if ever surfaced as an entry's body text in a future timeline view.

## R4 — Rendering the prototype's actual "Erro" states, closing RF01's documented carve-out

- **Decision**: `CaptureFailureBand` (specs/003's deliberately plain placeholder — generic message + one
  outline "Tentar de novo" button, no icon) is removed from `capture_status_views.dart`. A new
  `RecognitionErrorView` widget renders prototype-extract.md §2.3's actual "Erro" shape: a
  `sizeStatusIcon`-sized warning icon in `colorError`, the exact copy ("Não foi possível transcrever" /
  "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto"), an outline "Tentar novamente" button, and — for Foto only — the
  secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". `CaptureLoadingIndicator` and `CapturePermissionDeniedMessage` are
  unchanged and keep serving their existing, still-applicable roles (the former embeds into the new
  "Processando"/"Processando OCR" layouts alongside the frozen waveform/thumbnail; the latter is untouched by
  this unit, since Idle/PermissionDenied/Recording/Captura states are RF01's, not RF02's, to redesign).
- **Rationale**: This is not a new judgment call so much as carrying out RF01's own research.md R11 (specs/
  003) to its stated conclusion: that entry explicitly named the "Erro" states as "RF02's screens to build,"
  not an open design question for this unit to re-litigate. spec.md's resolved Clarification 1 confirms it
  ("this unit replaces RF01's placeholder recognition UX... with the dedicated states the prototype
  defines").
- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping `CaptureFailureBand` around for some other, hypothetical use —
  rejected: nothing else in this codebase renders it once Áudio/Foto failures move to `RecognitionErrorView`,
  and keeping dead code around violates the "don't keep unused code for hypothetical future need" guidance
  this plan is held to; it is deleted outright, not deprecated.

## R5 — A save-call failure after successful recognition gets its own (non-prototype-named) state, not a reuse of "Erro"

- **Decision**: If `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase` fails (offline, or the `entries-create` call itself fails) after
  the user taps "Salvar" from "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" — or taps "Salvar só a foto" from "Foto — Erro" — the
  bloc emits a new `*SaveFailure` state (`InsertionModalAudioSaveFailure`/`InsertionModalFotoSaveFailure`,
  data-model.md) that keeps the reviewed/edited text (and, for photo, the thumbnail) on screen with an inline
  error message, rather than falling back to the recognition-failure "Erro" state. Retrying is simply tapping
  "Salvar" (or "Salvar só a foto") again — no re-transcription, no re-OCR.
- **Rationale**: The prototype's "Erro" states (prototype-extract.md §2.3) are defined specifically for a
  *recognition* failure ("Não foi possível transcrever"/"...reconhecer o texto") — spec.md never describes a
  distinct screen for "recognition succeeded but the subsequent save failed," leaving this a genuine gap for
  reasonable technical judgment (Constitution Principle I). Falling back to "Erro" would be actively wrong
  here: it would discard the user's successfully-recognized (and possibly hand-edited) text to show a message
  about transcription/OCR, a step that already succeeded. This exactly mirrors an existing, already-approved
  precedent in this same codebase: the Texto tab's `InsertionModalTextoFailure` keeps the typed text visible
  and treats a second tap of the same "Salvar" button as its own retry (texto_tab_view.dart) — this unit
  applies that identical shape to Audio/Foto's post-review save step instead of inventing something new.
- **Alternatives considered**: Falling back silently to "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" with no visible error (just
  re-enabling "Salvar") — rejected: FR-009's "Erro" precedent and RNF09's "every write endpoint... handled" bar
  both imply the user must see *some* failure signal, not a silent no-op. Reusing "Erro" with its recognition
  copy substituted for a save-specific message — rejected as a confusing hybrid for the same reason RF01's own
  research.md R11 (specs/003) rejected partially borrowing a named state's look.

## R6 — Guarding against a stale recognition result after abandonment

- **Decision**: Before applying a `transcribe()`/`recognize()` result, the bloc re-checks that its *current*
  state is still the matching `*Processing` state for the same held file path (`_pendingAudioPath`/
  `_pendingImagePath` unchanged since the call started). If the user has since switched tabs, closed the
  modal, or (for photo) retried onto a different in-flight attempt, a late-arriving result is discarded
  outright — no state transition, no entry creation.
- **Rationale**: spec.md's User Story 5 / Edge Cases requires "no entry is created, regardless of how the
  in-flight recognition call eventually resolves," and FR-011 requires discarding "any in-progress
  recognition... held for that capture" on abandonment. Switching away from the Áudio/Foto tab already resets
  the *visible* state to that tab's idle state (mirroring RF01's existing tab-switch behavior), but without
  this explicit guard, a `transcribe()` call that resolves after the switch could still emit
  `InsertionModalAudioTranscribed`/`...Failure` and silently clobber whatever the user has navigated to since
  — a correctness bug even though `flutter_bloc` v9's post-`close()` emit is already a safe no-op (that only
  covers the modal-closed case, not the still-open-but-switched-tabs case).
- **Alternatives considered**: Cancelling the underlying `Future` itself (e.g., via a cancellation token passed
  into `whisper_ggml`/the OCR call) — rejected as disproportionate: neither `whisper_ggml` nor the OCR HTTP
  call exposes a cancellation hook, and the state-match guard achieves the same observable guarantee (no
  stray state/entry) without needing one.

## R7 — Consolidating `SaveAudioEntryUseCase`/`SavePhotoEntryUseCase` into one `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase`

- **Decision**: Once recognition is removed from each (R1, and photo's OCR step moving into the new
  `RecognizePhotoUseCase`, R-nothing-new beyond what data-model.md documents), `SaveAudioEntryUseCase` and
  `SavePhotoEntryUseCase` become identical in every line except the hardcoded `EntrySource` they pass to
  `CreateEntryUseCase`. Both are deleted and replaced by one `ConfirmEntrySaveUseCase(content, source)` —
  connectivity check, then `CreateEntryUseCase(content, source)` — used for Audio-Salvar, Foto-Salvar, and
  Foto-"Salvar só a foto" alike (the last simply supplies R3's placeholder string as `content`).
- **Rationale**: This is the one place in this unit where two call sites really would be pure duplication of
  each other, which is exactly the case where collapsing them is the right amount of abstraction (not a
  premature one) — "three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction" cuts the other way once the
  lines are not merely similar but identical modulo one parameter already present in the call signature.
- **Alternatives considered**: Keeping two thin per-modality usecases "for clarity/discoverability" —
  rejected: there is no behavioral difference left to name separately once `EntrySource` is just a parameter,
  and two near-identical classes are harder to keep in sync (e.g., a future RNF09 fix applied to one and
  missed in the other) than one.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
2	
3	**Branch**: `004-stt-ocr-processing` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec header)
4	
5	**Date**: 2026-10-13 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

8	§1 (RF02), §6.2 (`/media/ocr`, `/entries`), §13 (technical constraints), `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`

13

15	and `POST /entries` — but fused each modality's recognition and entry-creation into one atomic, auto-saving

18	"Reconhecendo texto..." states (prototype-extract.md §2.3), and lands on an editable review state
